definition_en: the place where someone lives, or the fact of living there
core_image: 一扇亮着灯的窗，窗后是某人固定的家
scene: 总统官邸位于河岸边，四周有高高的围栏。The president's residence stands by the river, surrounded by high fences.
sceneCN: 这里 residence 是「官邸；住宅」（第 1 个义项：某人居住的地方）；句意：总统官邸位于河岸边，四周有高高的围栏。

senses.title: The place where someone lives
senses.definition: the house or place in which a person lives
senses.definitionCN: 一个人居住的房子或地方
senses.example: The president's residence stands by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 总统官邸位于河岸边。
senses.why: The noun names the place produced by residing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指居住这一行为所产生的场所。

senses.title: The act or period of living somewhere
senses.definition: the fact of living in a place, often used in official language
senses.definitionCN: 在某地居住的事实，常用于官方语言
senses.example: She took up residence in Paris last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年开始在巴黎居住。
senses.why: Residence can name the state of living there, not only the building.
senses.whyCN: residence 可指居住状态，而不只是建筑。

senses.title: A large impressive house
senses.definition: a large and formal house, especially an official one
senses.definitionCN: 大型而正式的住宅，尤指官邸
senses.example: The family moved to a smaller residence.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人搬进了一处较小的宅邸。
senses.why: The formal word for a home often suggests size and dignity.
senses.whyCN: 「住所」的正式说法常带有规模与体面的意味。

intro.en: Residence comes from Latin residentia, a staying behind, from residere, to remain, through Old French residence.
intro.cn: residence 来自拉丁语 residentia（停留），源于 residere（留下），经古法语 residence 进入英语。

items.en: Sedere means to sit.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐。

items.en: Residere means to remain behind or dwell.
items.cn: residere 意为留下、居住。

items.en: Residentia means a staying behind or a dwelling.
items.cn: residentia 意为停留、居所。

items.en: Residence means a place of dwelling.
items.cn: residence 意为居住之处。

items.en: English residence names both the act and the place of living.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，英语 residence 兼指居住行为与住所。

items.en: Modern English uses residence for homes, permits, and official dwellings.
items.cn: 现代英语中，residence 用于住宅、居留许可与官邸。

note.en: Residence is the noun of residing, and it sits near its family and near words for home and dwelling.
note.cn: residence 是 reside 的名词，与自身词族以及表示家和住所的词相邻。

senses.example: The residents of the street meet every spring.

senses.title: A doctor in hospital training
senses.definition: a doctor who has finished medical school and is training in a hospital
senses.definitionCN: 医学院毕业后在医院接受培训的医生
senses.example: She is a resident doctor at the city hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 她是市医院的住院医生。
senses.why: The doctor lives at the hospital during training, so the residing word fits the role.
senses.whyCN: 这类医生在培训期间住在医院，因此「居住」这个词也适用于这一身份。

senses.title: Living in a place
senses.definition: living permanently in a particular place, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 长期住在某处，用于名词前

senses.exampleCN: 一只常驻的猫睡在炉火旁。

senses.whyCN: 形容词描述长期待在那里而非临时来访的人或动物。

senses.title: Consisting of homes

senses.example: They live in a quiet residential area.

senses.why: Any building can be classified by whether it is meant for living in.

definition_en: to officially leave a job, or to accept something you cannot change
core_image: 一个人把办公室钥匙放在桌上，签下最后一笔
scene: 董事会改组后，财务总监当天就递交了辞呈。After the board was reshuffled, the finance director resigned that same day.
sceneCN: 这里 resign 是「辞职」（第 1 个义项：正式离开职位）；句意：董事会改组后，财务总监当天就辞职了。

senses.title: To leave a job officially
senses.definition: to state formally that you are leaving your job or position
senses.definitionCN: 正式声明将要离开工作或职位
senses.example: The finance director resigned that same day.
senses.exampleCN: 财务总监当天就辞职了。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to unseal or give back, and giving back a post is the modern core.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为开封交回，而把职位交回就是现代核心义。

senses.title: To give up a right or claim
senses.definition: to surrender a right, claim, or possession formally
senses.definitionCN: 正式让出权利、主张或所有物
senses.example: She resigned her claim to the property.
senses.exampleCN: 她放弃了对这处房产的继承主张。
senses.why: What is given back can be a right as well as a job.
senses.whyCN: 交回的既可以是职位，也可以是权利。

senses.title: To accept what cannot be changed
senses.definition: to accept an unpleasant situation because it cannot be avoided
senses.definitionCN: 因无法避免而接受不愉快的处境
senses.example: He resigned himself to another long wait.
senses.exampleCN: 他只好认命，再等下去。
senses.why: Giving up resistance inward produces the reflexive sense of resigning oneself.
senses.whyCN: 在内心里放弃抵抗，就产生「使自己顺从」的反身义项。

intro.en: Resign comes from Latin resignare, to unseal or cancel, from re- and signare, to mark with a sign.
intro.cn: resign 来自拉丁语 resignare（开封、注销），由 re- 与 signare（作标记）构成。

items.en: Signare means to mark or seal.
items.cn: signare 意为标记或盖章。

items.en: Resignare means to unseal or cancel a document.
items.cn: resignare 意为开封或注销文书。

items.en: Resigner means to resign or give up.
items.cn: resigner 意为辞去、放弃。

items.en: Middle English resignen means to give up a claim.
items.cn: 中古英语 resignen 意为放弃主张。

items.en: Resign is used for leaving an office.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，resign 用于离开职位。

items.en: Modern English extends resign to accepting what cannot be changed.
items.cn: 现代英语把 resign 扩展到接受无法改变之事。

note.en: Resign is a handing-back verb, and it sits near its family and near verbs for quitting and surrendering.
note.cn: resign 是一个「交回」动词，与自身词族以及表示退出和让出的动词相邻。

normal.cn: resignation 既指辞职行为，也指辞呈。

normal.en: Compare quit: quit is informal, while resign is official.
normal.cn: 对比 quit：quit 口语化，resign 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a key placed on a desk beside a signed letter.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙放在桌上，旁边是一封签好的信。

abstract.en: Imagine a name being crossed off a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门上的名字被划掉。

abstract.en: Think of a knot loosened rather than cut.
abstract.cn: 想象绳结被慢慢松开，而不是剪断。

examples.en: The finance director resigned that same day.
examples.cn: 财务总监当天就辞职了。

examples.en: She resigned her claim to the property.
examples.cn: 她放弃了对这处房产的继承主张。

examples.en: He resigned himself to another long wait.
examples.cn: 他只好认命，再等下去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + sign」——再次签字，把职位交回，就是辞职；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 signare（标记）→ resignare（开封、注销）→ 古法语 resigner → 中古英语 resignen → 现代英语 resign。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with formally handing something back, applies it to jobs and claims, and finally turns inward to accepting what cannot be changed.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从正式交回某物开始，用于职位与主张，最后转向内心，表示接受无法改变之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key and a signed paper left on a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙与签好的文件留在桌上。

branches.en: Leaving a post is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 离开职位，是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Giving up a right is the same handover in law.
branches.cn: 放弃权利，是法律中的同一种交回。

branches.en: Accepting the unavoidable is a handover inside the mind.
branches.cn: 接受不可避免之事，是内心里的交回。

branches.en: A post and a claim can both be formally given back.
branches.cn: 职位与主张都可以正式交回。

branches.en: Giving up a claim and giving up struggle lead to the same quiet.
branches.cn: 放弃主张与放弃挣扎通向同一种平静。

intro.en: Resign is a Latin verb carried through French, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: resign 是经法语传递的拉丁动词，词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin signare means to mark or seal, and resignare means to unseal or cancel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signare 意为标记或盖章，resignare 意为开封或注销。

items.example: Re- adds the idea of giving back.
Resignare joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: resignare 把前缀与词根结合。

items.example: Resigner carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: resigner 把这个动词带入法语。

items.meaning: the act or letter of resigning

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

definition_en: the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties, or of a system to absorb disturbance and return to its previous state or function
core_image: 被压弯的芦苇在风停后弹回原位
scene: 洪水退去后，这片芦苇地在两个季节内恢复了原有高度与盖度，显示出很强的恢复力。 After the flood receded, this reed bed recovered its former height and cover within two seasons, showing strong resilience.
sceneCN: 这里 resilience 是「恢复力」（第 1 个义项：受扰后回到原状态的能力）；句意：洪水退去后，这片芦苇地在两个季节内恢复了原有高度与盖度，显示出很强的恢复力。

pos.zh: 恢复力；韧性；回弹能力（多作不可数）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多种恢复力）

derivatives.zh: 弹回；撤回（法律与正式用语）

senses.title: Ecological capacity to absorb disturbance
senses.titleCN: 生态学上的吸收扰动能力
senses.definition: the capacity of an ecosystem to absorb disturbance and keep its structure and functions
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统吸收扰动并保持结构与功能的能力
senses.example: Coral reef resilience depends on herbivorous fish and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁的恢复力依赖植食性鱼类与清洁的水。
senses.why: From Latin resilire 'to leap back', resilience is the ability to be pushed and still spring back into the same shape.
senses.whyCN: 来自拉丁语 resilire「跳回」，resilience 就是被推之后仍弹回原形的能力。

senses.title: Engineering return time
senses.definition: the speed with which a system returns to equilibrium after a displacement
senses.definitionCN: 系统被推离后回到平衡的速度
senses.example: Engineering resilience measures how quickly the lake clears after a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 工程恢复力度量湖泊在风暴后多快恢复清澈。
senses.why: In engineering, resilience is a stopwatch: the faster the return, the more resilient the system. Ecology later distinguished this from the ability to absorb change at all.
senses.whyCN: 在工程学中，resilience 是秒表：回归越快，系统越有恢复力。生态学后来把它与“能否吸收变化”区分开。

senses.title: Psychological resilience
senses.definition: the capacity of a person to cope with stress, loss, or adversity and continue functioning
senses.definitionCN: 个人应对压力、丧失或逆境并继续运作的能力
senses.example: Children's resilience after displacement depended on stable caregivers.
senses.exampleCN: 流离失所后儿童的心理韧性取决于稳定的照护者。
senses.why: The physical image of springing back is applied to the mind: adversity bends a person, and resilience is the return, not the absence of bending.
senses.whyCN: 弹回的物理意象被用于心理：逆境把人压弯，resilience 是回归，而不是从未被压弯。

senses.title: Material resilience
senses.definition: the ability of a material to return to its original shape after being bent or compressed
senses.definitionCN: 材料被弯曲或压缩后恢复原形的能力
senses.example: The resilience of the reed fibres makes the mat spring back.
senses.exampleCN: 芦苇纤维的回弹性使垫子能弹回。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal layer: resiliens described something leaping back, and materials still demonstrate the original image most directly.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面层：resiliens 描述某物跳回，而材料至今最直接地展示这一原始意象。

senses.title: Community or social resilience
senses.definition: the capacity of a community to prepare for, respond to, and recover from shocks
senses.definitionCN: 社区准备、应对并从冲击中恢复的能力
senses.example: Neighbour networks increased the town's resilience to the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 邻里网络提高了小镇对洪水的韧性。
senses.why: The unit changes from an individual to a community; the 'springing back' now depends on social ties, infrastructure, and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 单位从个人变为社区；“弹回”现在依赖社会纽带、基础设施与制度。

senses.title: Organizational or business resilience
senses.definition: the capacity of an organization to withstand disruption and continue its core functions
senses.definitionCN: 组织承受中断并继续核心职能的能力
senses.example: Supply-chain resilience became a board-level concern after the pandemic.
senses.exampleCN: 疫情之后，供应链韧性成为董事会层面的议题。
senses.why: The collective unit changes again: an organization must keep its core functions when suppliers, staff, or systems fail.
senses.whyCN: 集体单位再次变化：当供应商、员工或系统失效时，组织必须维持核心职能。

senses.title: Resilience contrasted with resistance
senses.titleCN: 恢复力与抵抗力的对照
senses.definition: the property of recovering after change, as opposed to resisting change in the first place
senses.definitionCN: 变化后恢复的属性，与首先抵抗变化的属性相对
senses.example: A resistant forest barely changes; a resilient one changes and returns.
senses.exampleCN: 有抵抗力的森林几乎不变；有恢复力的森林会变化然后回归。
senses.why: The pair divides the labour of stability: resistance refuses the push, resilience accepts it and comes back.
senses.whyCN: 这一对概念分担了稳定性的工作：抵抗力拒绝推力，恢复力接受推力再回来。

senses.title: Resilience as a policy goal
senses.titleCN: 作为政策目标的恢复力
senses.definition: a desired capacity that governments, insurers, and planners try to measure and increase
senses.definitionCN: 政府、保险机构与规划者试图度量并提升的理想能力
senses.example: The city plan set a resilience target for heat waves.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划为热浪设定了韧性目标。
senses.why: When a concept becomes a target, it is operationalized: indicators, audits, and budgets turn 'springing back' into something to be managed.
senses.whyCN: 当概念成为目标，它就被操作化：指标、审计与预算把“弹回”变成可管理的东西。

intro.en: Resilience comes from Latin resiliens, the present participle of resilire 'to leap back', from re- 'back' + salire 'to leap'. The same salire gives result and assault.
intro.cn: resilience 来自拉丁语 resiliens，即 resilire「跳回」的现在分词，由 re-「向后」+ salire「跳」构成。同一个 salire 还衍生 result 与 assault。

items.en: resilire 'to rebound, recoil, leap back' = re- 'back' + salire 'to leap, jump'. Its participle resiliens is the direct source of the English noun and adjective.
items.cn: resilire「弹回、反冲、跳回」= re-「向后」+ salire「跳」。其分词 resiliens 是英语名词与形容词的直接来源。

items.en: English resilience is recorded in the seventeenth century, first for the physical property of springing back.
items.cn: 英语 resilience 于 17 世纪被记录，最初指物体弹回的物理属性。

items.en: The word extended to character: a resilient person recovers from hardship as a bent rod recovers its shape.
items.cn: 该词扩展到性格：有韧性的人从困苦中恢复，正如弯曲的杆恢复形状。

items.en: Ecology adopted resilience for the capacity to absorb disturbance; C. S. Holling distinguished it from resistance and from engineering return time.
items.cn: 生态学采用 resilience 指吸收扰动的能力；Holling 把它与抵抗力和工程回归时间区分开。

items.en: Modern usage spans materials, psychology, ecology, disaster planning, and business; the noun is usually uncountable.
items.cn: 现代用法横跨材料、心理学、生态学、灾害规划与商业；该名词通常不可数。

note.en: The first group separates resilience terms, the second compares capacities under stress.
note.cn: 第一组区分恢复力术语，第二组比较压力下的能力。

entries.definition: having resilience; the adjective describes the bearer, the noun the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 具有恢复力的；形容词描述承载者，名词描述能力。

entries.definition: an American variant of resilience, chiefly in psychology and policy writing.
entries.definitionCN: resilience 的美式变体，主要用于心理学与政策写作。

entries.definition: to spring back or withdraw, chiefly in legal usage.
entries.definitionCN: 弹回或撤回，主要用于法律语境。

entries.definition: an outcome, literally 'that which springs back'; it shares salire but not the 'recover' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 结果，字面为“弹回之物”；共享 salire，但无“恢复”义。

entries.definition: the capacity to withstand a push without being displaced.
entries.definitionCN: 承受推力而不被推离的能力。

entries.definition: the ability to keep functioning across a range of conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 在一系列条件下持续运作的能力。

entries.definition: the ability to absorb energy without breaking; it is about not failing, not about returning.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收能量而不破坏的能力；关乎不失效，而非回归。

entries.definition: the capacity to adjust to new conditions rather than return to old ones.
entries.definitionCN: 调整以适应新条件、而非回到旧状态的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin leap, standard phrases, and real contrasts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语“跳”的意象、标准搭配与真实对比。

normal.en: re- + salire: to leap back. Resilience is the leap back after being bent.
normal.cn: re- + salire：向后跳。resilience 是被压弯后的那一跳。

normal.en: Result and assault share salire: one springs back, the other leaps at.
normal.cn: result 与 assault 共享 salire：一个弹回，一个扑向。

normal.en: Resistance refuses the push; resilience takes it and returns.
normal.cn: 抵抗力拒绝推力；恢复力接受推力并回归。

normal.en: Psychological resilience is not 'never bending'; it is bending and coming back.
normal.cn: 心理韧性不是“从不弯曲”，而是弯曲后再回来。

normal.en: Engineering resilience is measured by return time; ecological resilience by the ability to absorb change.
normal.cn: 工程恢复力以回归时间度量；生态恢复力以吸收变化的能力度量。

abstract.en: Picture a reed in wind: it bends almost flat, then stands up when the gust passes. That stand-up is resilience.
abstract.cn: 想象风中的芦苇：它几乎被压平，阵风过后又立起来。这个“立起来”就是 resilience。

abstract.en: The word always implies a prior disturbance; without a push there is nothing to spring back from.
abstract.cn: 这个词总隐含先前的扰动；没有推力，就无所谓弹回。

abstract.en: A system can be resilient and still change: returning to function is not the same as returning to the exact old state.
abstract.cn: 系统可以有恢复力却仍发生变化：回到功能不等于回到完全旧状态。

examples.en: The reef's resilience declined as water temperatures rose.
examples.cn: 随着水温升高，该礁的恢复力下降。

examples.en: Community resilience depends on trust as much as on concrete barriers.
examples.cn: 社区韧性既依赖混凝土屏障，也依赖信任。

examples.en: Engineers measure resilience as the time a network needs to recover.
examples.cn: 工程师把恢复力度量为一个网络恢复所需的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞贼连斯”——被压弯了还能连着弹回来 → resilience 恢复力、韧性

root: 拉丁语 resilire「跳回」，re-（向后）+ salire（跳）；同根词有 result、assault、salient。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of resilience: ecological absorption, engineering return time, psychological coping, material spring-back, community and organizational capacity, the contrast with resistance, and the same capacity used as a policy target.
sensesIntro.cn: resilience 的八个义项：生态吸收、工程回归时间、心理应对、材料回弹、社区与组织能力、与抵抗力的对照，以及作为政策目标的同一能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bent reed springs upright when the wind stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：被压弯的芦苇在风停后弹直。

branches.en: ECOLOGY: the capacity to absorb disturbance and keep the same relationships.
branches.cn: 生态学：吸收扰动并保持原有关系格局的能力。

branches.en: CONTRAST: resilience is coming back, resistance is not moving at all.
branches.cn: 对照：恢复力是回到原状，抵抗力是根本不被推动。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: the stopwatch version, measured as return time.
branches.cn: 工程学：用秒表计时的版本，以回归时间度量。

branches.en: PERSON AND MATERIAL: minds and fibres both bend and come back.
branches.cn: 人与材料：心理与纤维都会弯曲再回弹。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND POLICY: communities, firms, and governments turn resilience into a target.
branches.cn: 集体与政策：社区、企业与政府把恢复力变成目标。

intro.en: Resilience is Latin re- + salire plus the noun suffix -ence. English also forms resilient, resile, and the variant resiliency; salire is a bound Latin stem.
intro.cn: resilience 是拉丁语 re- + salire 加名词后缀 -ence。英语还构成 resilient、resile 与变体 resiliency；salire 是黏着拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin salire 'to leap' yields resilient, resilience, resile, result, assault, and salient; the re- prefix marks a backward direction in the resilient branch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 salire「跳」衍生 resilient、resilience、resile、result、assault、salient；re- 前缀在 resilient 一支标记向后方向。

items.meaningCN: 弹回的；有韧性的（-ent 形容词）
items.exampleCN: 有韧性的作物能熬过干旱。

items.example: The contract resiled to earlier terms.

items.meaning: that which springs back; an outcome

definition_en: to fight against something, or to stop yourself from doing something
core_image: 双手撑住一扇被猛推的门，不让它关上
scene: 居民联合起来反对在公园里建停车场。Residents joined together to resist the plan for a car park in the park.
sceneCN: 这里 resist 是「抵制」（第 1 个义项：反对并试图阻止）；句意：居民联合起来抵制在公园里建停车场的计划。

senses.title: To fight against something
senses.definition: to act against a force, plan, or person that tries to control you
senses.definitionCN: 对试图控制你的力量、计划或人采取对抗行动
senses.example: Residents joined together to resist the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 居民联合起来抵制这项计划。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to stand against, and standing firm is the core image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「站到对面」，站稳是核心意象。

senses.title: To refuse to accept
senses.definition: to refuse to accept a change, idea, or influence
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝接受某种变化、观念或影响
senses.example: Many staff resisted the new rules at first.
senses.exampleCN: 许多员工起初抗拒新规定。
senses.why: Standing against can be mental as well as physical.
senses.whyCN: 「站到对面」既可以是身体的，也可以是心理的。

senses.title: To stop yourself doing something
senses.definition: to stop yourself from doing something you want to do
senses.definitionCN: 阻止自己去做想做的事
senses.example: She could not resist the temptation to laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 她忍不住笑了出来。
senses.why: The urge is an inner push, and resisting is the self standing against it.
senses.whyCN: 冲动是一种内在推力，而抵抗就是自我顶住它。

intro.en: Resist comes from Latin resistere, to stand against, from re- and sistere, to take a stand.
intro.cn: resist 来自拉丁语 resistere（站到对面），由 re- 与 sistere（站定）构成。

items.en: Sistere means to cause to stand or take a stand.
items.cn: sistere 意为使站立、站定。

items.en: Resistere means to stand against or withstand.
items.cn: resistere 意为站到对面、抵挡。

items.en: Resister means to resist or oppose.
items.cn: resister 意为抵抗、反对。

items.en: Middle English resisten keeps the sense of standing firm.
items.cn: 中古英语 resisten 保留「站稳」的意思。

items.en: Resist covers both physical and moral opposition.
items.cn: 到 15 世纪，resist 兼指身体与道德上的对抗。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of resisting temptation.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「抵抗诱惑」的义项。

note.en: Resist is a standing-against verb, and it sits near its family and near verbs for opposing and withstanding.
note.cn: resist 是一个「站到对面」的动词，与自身词族以及表示反对和抵挡的动词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of resisting or a force against motion
able to withstand something
a device that limits electric current
to disagree with and try to stop something
to be strong enough to bear a force
to say that you will not do something

normalIntro.en: Resist contains Latin sistere, to stand: to resist is to stand against pressure.
normalIntro.cn: resist 含有拉丁语 sistere（站）：抵抗就是顶着压力站稳。

normal.en: Re- means back or against, and sistere means stand.
normal.cn: re- 表示回或对抗，sistere 表示站。

normal.en: Resist change is a common phrase in organisations.
normal.cn: resist change 是组织中的常见说法。

normal.en: Resist temptation is the inner version of standing firm.
normal.cn: resist temptation 是「站稳」的内心版本。

normal.en: Resistance is the noun, and resistant is the adjective.
normal.cn: resistance 是名词，resistant 是形容词。

normal.en: Compare oppose: oppose can be verbal, while resist often involves action.
normal.cn: 对比 oppose：oppose 可以是口头的，resist 常涉及行动。

abstract.en: Picture both hands braced against a closing door.
abstract.cn: 想象双手撑住一扇正在关上的门。

abstract.en: Imagine feet planted while a crowd pushes forward.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚钉住，人群却往前推。

abstract.en: Think of a guard holding a rope taut.
abstract.cn: 想象守卫把绳子绷得笔直。

examples.en: Residents joined together to resist the plan.
examples.cn: 居民联合起来抵制这项计划。

examples.en: She could not resist the temptation to laugh.
examples.cn: 她忍不住笑了出来。

examples.en: The material resists heat well.
examples.cn: 这种材料很耐热。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + sist」——站稳了往回顶，就是抵抗；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sistere（站定）→ resistere（站到对面）→ 古法语 resister → 中古英语 resisten → 现代英语 resist。

sensesIntro.en: The verb pictures standing against a push: against a plan, against an idea, and against one's own urge.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词描绘顶住推力：顶住计划、顶住观念，也顶住自己的冲动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet planted and hands braced against a push.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚钉住，双手撑住一股推力。

branches.en: Acting against an external force is the core sense.
branches.cn: 对抗外部力量，是核心义项。

branches.en: Refusing a change is the mental form of standing firm.
branches.cn: 拒绝变化，是站稳的心理形式。

branches.en: Resisting an urge is standing against an inner push.
branches.cn: 忍住冲动，是顶住内在推力。

branches.en: A plan resisted in public and in private uses the same image.
branches.cn: 公开与私下抵制计划使用同一意象。

branches.en: Rejecting an idea and controlling an urge both require strength.
branches.cn: 拒绝观念与控制冲动都需要力量。

intro.en: Resist is a Latin verb carried through French, with English endings forming its modern family.
intro.cn: resist 是经法语传递的拉丁动词，现代词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere means to take a stand, and resistere means to stand against.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere 意为站定，resistere 意为站到对面。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of pushing back.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「顶回去」的意思。

definition_en: the act of fighting against something, or a force that slows something down
core_image: 一股力量顶住另一股力量，谁也无法轻易前进
scene: 这种细菌对常见抗生素产生了耐药性。The bacteria have developed resistance to common antibiotics.
sceneCN: 这里 resistance 是「耐药性」（第 3 个义项：对药物不再敏感）；句意：这种细菌对常见抗生素产生了耐药性。

senses.title: The act of opposing
senses.definition: the act of fighting against a person, plan, or system
senses.definitionCN: 对抗某人、计划或制度的行为
senses.example: The plan met with strong resistance from residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划遭到居民的强烈抵抗。
senses.why: The noun names the standing-against itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指「站到对面」这一行为本身。

senses.title: A force that slows motion
senses.definition: a physical force that opposes movement, or the property that limits electric current
senses.definitionCN: 阻碍运动的物理力，或限制电流的性质
senses.example: The wire has low electrical resistance.
senses.exampleCN: 这根导线的电阻很低。
senses.why: Physical resistance is the same opposition seen in materials and circuits.
senses.whyCN: 物理阻力是同样的「对抗」在材料与电路中的体现。

senses.title: The ability to withstand disease or drugs
senses.definition: the ability of a body, plant, or germ to remain unharmed by a disease or drug
senses.definitionCN: 身体、植物或病菌不受疾病或药物伤害的能力
senses.example: The bacteria have developed resistance to common antibiotics.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细菌对常见抗生素产生了耐药性。
senses.why: A living thing standing against attack is resistance in the biological sense.
senses.whyCN: 生物顶住侵害，就是生物学意义上的抵抗。

intro.en: Resistance comes from Latin resistere, to stand against, through Old French, with the English noun ending -ance.
intro.cn: resistance 来自拉丁语 resistere（站到对面），经古法语进入英语，加名词词尾 -ance。

items.en: Sistere means to take a stand.
items.cn: sistere 意为站定。

items.en: Resistere means to stand against.
items.cn: resistere 意为站到对面。

items.en: Resister means to resist or oppose.
items.cn: resister 意为抵抗、反对。

items.en: Middle English resisten gives the base verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 resisten 提供基础动词。

items.en: Resistance appears as the act of resisting.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，resistance 指抵抗行为。

items.en: Physical and electrical resistance become standard scientific terms.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，物理阻力与电阻成为标准科学术语。

note.en: Resistance is the noun of resist, and it sits near its family and near words for opposition and immunity.
note.cn: resistance 是 resist 的名词，与自身词族以及表示对抗和免疫的词相邻。

senses.title: Not easily harmed by something
senses.definition: strong enough to remain undamaged or unaffected by a substance or condition
senses.definitionCN: 足够坚固，面对某种物质或条件仍不受损、不受影响
senses.example: This cloth is treated to be resistant to water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种布经过处理，能防水。
senses.why: The -ant adjective describes the quality shown by something that resists.
senses.whyCN: -ant 形容词描述某物抵抗时所展现的性质。

senses.title: Opposing change or control
senses.definition: unwilling to accept a change, idea, or authority
senses.definitionCN: 不愿接受变化、观念或权威
senses.example: The committee was resistant to change.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会抗拒变革。

senses.whyCN: 同样的「顶住」性质出现在人的态度中。

senses.title: Able to withstand a drug
senses.definition: used of germs that are no longer harmed by a medicine
senses.definitionCN: 用于指不再被药物伤害的病菌
senses.example: Drug-resistant bacteria are a growing concern.
senses.exampleCN: 耐药细菌日益令人担忧。
senses.why: A germ that stands against medicine is resistant in the medical sense.
senses.whyCN: 顶住药物的病菌，就是医学意义上的「耐药」。

normal.en: People can be resistant to change.

abstract.en: Imagine a shield taking a blow without cracking.

abstract.en: Think of weeds pushing back through pavement.

definition_en: a firm decision, a formal vote, the solving of a problem, or image sharpness
core_image: 一个人把复杂纠缠的线团一点点解开，最后拉直
scene: 新年第一天，她下定决心每天早起读书。On the first day of the new year, she made a resolution to read every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 resolution 是「决心」（第 1 个义项：坚定的决定）；句意：新年第一天，她下定决心每天早起读书。

senses.title: A firm personal decision
senses.definition: a serious decision to do or stop doing something
senses.definitionCN: 认真决定去做或停止做某事
senses.example: She made a resolution to read every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她下定决心每天早晨读书。
senses.why: The word names the mind settling on a course, like a knot finally pulled straight.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指心思终于定下方向，就像绳结最终被拉直。

senses.title: A formal decision by vote
senses.definition: a formal statement or decision agreed by a group or council
senses.definitionCN: 由团体或委员会表决同意的正式声明或决定
senses.example: The council passed a resolution against the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会通过了一项反对该计划的决议。
senses.why: A group can settle its will as firmly as a person does.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体也能像个人一样坚定地定下意志。

senses.title: The solving of a problem
senses.definition: the act of finding an answer to a difficulty or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 为困难或争端找到答案的行为
senses.example: The resolution of the dispute took months.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端的解决花了几个月。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to loosen, and solving a problem is loosening it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为松开，而解决问题就是把问题松开。

senses.title: Image sharpness
senses.definition: the amount of detail a screen, image, or lens can show
senses.definitionCN: 屏幕、图像或镜头能显示的细节数量
senses.example: The photograph has very high resolution.
senses.exampleCN: 这张照片的分辨率很高。
senses.why: A high-resolution image can be resolved, or separated, into fine points of detail.
senses.whyCN: 高分辨率图像能被「解析」成细小的细节点。

intro.en: Resolution comes from Latin resolutio, a loosening, from resolvere, to loosen completely, built on re- and solvere.
intro.cn: resolution 来自拉丁语 resolutio（松开），源于 resolvere（彻底解开），由 re- 与 solvere 构成。

items.en: Solvere means to loosen, release, or pay.
items.cn: solvere 意为松开、释放或偿付。

items.en: Resolvere means to loosen completely or dissolve.
items.cn: resolvere 意为彻底解开或溶解。

items.en: Resolutio means a loosening or a settling.
items.cn: resolutio 意为松开、定解。

items.en: Resolution keeps the sense of a firm settling.
items.cn: resolution 保留「坚定定下」的含义。

items.en: Middle English resolution covers decisions and solutions.
items.cn: 中古英语 resolution 兼指决定与解决。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of screen and image sharpness.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了屏幕与图像分辨率的义项。

note.en: Resolution is the noun of resolve, and it sits near its family and near words for decision and solution.
note.cn: resolution 是 resolve 的名词，与自身词族以及表示决定和解决的词相邻。

abstract.cn: 想象一团乱绳被一缕缕理直。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pressing a stamp on a formal paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在正式文件上盖章。

abstract.en: Think of a blurred photo sharpening into clear faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一张模糊照片渐渐显出清晰的面孔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tangled problem loosened until it lies straight.

branches.en: A personal decision is the mind settling on one course.

branches.en: A formal vote settles a group's will.

branches.en: Solving a problem loosens its difficulties.
branches.cn: 解决问题就是把难处解开。

branches.en: Image sharpness separates a picture into fine points.

definition_en: to solve a problem, or to decide firmly to do something
core_image: 把一团乱麻一根根解开，直到线变得笔直
scene: 两家人坐下来谈了一个下午，终于把多年的地界纠纷解决了。The two families sat down for an afternoon and finally resolved their long dispute over the boundary.
sceneCN: 这里 resolve 是「解决」（第 1 个义项：把问题处理掉）；句意：两家人坐了一个下午，终于解决了多年的地界纠纷。

senses.title: To solve a problem or end a dispute
senses.definition: to find an answer to a problem or bring a disagreement to an end
senses.definitionCN: 为问题找到答案，或结束分歧
senses.example: The two families resolved their dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 两家人解决了他们的争端。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to loosen, and a solved problem is a loosened knot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为松开，被解决的问题就是被解开的结。

senses.title: To decide firmly
senses.definition: to make a firm decision to do something
senses.definitionCN: 坚定决定去做某事
senses.example: She resolved to speak to him that evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她决心那天晚上和他谈一谈。
senses.why: A mind that stops wavering has settled, or resolved itself, on one course.
senses.whyCN: 不再摇摆的心思就「定」在了一条路上。

senses.title: To separate into parts
senses.definition: to break down or change into separate parts, used in technical description
senses.definitionCN: 分解或转变为不同部分，用于技术描写
senses.example: The mixture resolved into two clear layers.
senses.exampleCN: 混合物分成了两层清澈的液体。
senses.why: Loosening can mean a whole separating into its components.
senses.whyCN: 「松开」也可以指整体分开成各个组成部分。

intro.cn: resolve 来自拉丁语 resolvere（彻底解开），由 re- 与 solvere（松开）构成。

items.en: Solvere means to loosen or release.
items.cn: solvere 意为松开、释放。

items.en: Resolvere means to loosen completely or dissolve.

items.en: Resolutus is the past participle, loosened or settled.
items.cn: resolutus 是过去分词，意为已解开、已定下。

items.en: Resolver means to resolve or settle.
items.cn: resolver 意为解决、定下。

items.en: Middle English resolven covers solving and deciding.
items.cn: 中古英语 resolven 兼指解决与决定。

items.en: Modern English adds the technical sense of separating into parts.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「分解为部分」的技术义项。

note.en: Resolve is a loosening verb, and it sits near its family and near verbs for solving and deciding.
note.cn: resolve 是一个「松开」动词，与自身词族以及表示解决和决定的动词相邻。

entries.definition: a decision, vote, or solution
firmly decided
firm and determined
to find the answer to a problem
to choose after thinking
to end a disagreement

normalIntro.en: Resolve contains solvere, to loosen: solving a problem is loosening a knot.
normalIntro.cn: resolve 含有 solvere（松开）：解决问题就是解开一个结。

normal.en: Re- means back or completely, and solvere means loosen.
normal.cn: re- 表示回或彻底，solvere 表示松开。

normal.en: Resolve a dispute is the common phrase.
normal.cn: resolve a dispute 是常见短语。

normal.en: Resolve to do something means decide firmly.
normal.cn: resolve to do something 意为坚定决定去做。

normal.en: The noun is resolution, the same loosening.
normal.cn: 名词是 resolution，同样是「解开」。

normal.en: Compare solve: solve finds the answer, while resolve often ends a conflict.
normal.cn: 对比 solve：solve 找出答案，resolve 常结束冲突。

abstract.en: Picture a knot loosening under patient fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象绳结在耐心的手指下慢慢松开。

abstract.en: Imagine two people shaking hands after a long argument.
abstract.cn: 想象两人长谈后握手言和。

abstract.en: Think of muddy water settling until it is clear.
abstract.cn: 想象浑水渐渐沉淀变清。

examples.en: The two families resolved their dispute.
examples.cn: 两家人解决了他们的争端。

examples.en: She resolved to speak to him that evening.
examples.cn: 她决心那天晚上和他谈一谈。

examples.en: The mixture resolved into two clear layers.
examples.cn: 混合物分成了两层清澈的液体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + solve」——回头把问题松开、解开，就是解决；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 solvere（松开）→ resolvere（彻底解开）→ 古法语 resolver → 中古英语 resolven → 现代英语 resolve。

sensesIntro.en: The verb loosens a problem, settles a wavering mind, and can also describe a whole separating into layers.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词把问题松开、把摇摆的心思定下，也可描述整体分离成层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knot loosened until the cord lies flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳结被解开，绳子平直。

branches.en: Ending a problem is the core loosening sense.
branches.cn: 结束问题，是核心的「解开」义项。

branches.en: A firm decision settles the mind.
branches.cn: 坚定的决定让心思安定。

branches.en: Separating into parts is a whole coming loose.
branches.cn: 分解成部分，是整体松开。

branches.en: Solving and deciding both remove inner or outer confusion.
branches.cn: 解决与决定都消除内在或外在的混乱。

branches.en: A settled decision and a settled mixture both become clear.
branches.cn: 定下的决定与沉淀的混合物都变得清楚。

intro.en: Resolve is a Latin verb carried through French, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: resolve 是经法语传递的拉丁动词，词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere means to loosen, and resolvere means to loosen completely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solvere 意为松开，resolvere 意为彻底解开。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of loosening back.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「往回松开」的意思。

items.example: Resolvere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: resolvere 把前缀与词根结合。
resolutus 提供「已定下」的含义。

items.example: Resolver carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: resolver 把这个动词带入法语。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

items.example: Resolute shares the same Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: resolute 共享同一拉丁词干。

definition_zh: 共振；共鸣；洪亮的回响；物理学中系统在特定频率下的强响应
definition_en: a strong sympathetic vibration produced when a system is driven at its natural frequency, or the deep echoing quality of a sound
core_image: 一个长音正好撞上玻璃杯的固有节律，杯壁越摆越大，直到裂开
scene: 歌剧演员唱出一个长音，玻璃杯突然裂开。The glass shattered because the note matched its resonance exactly.
sceneCN: 这里 resonance 指「系统在固有频率下产生的强响应」（第 1 个义项：外驱频率与固有频率相合时的剧烈振动）；句意：玻璃杯碎裂，是因为那个音正好与它的共振频率相合。图中可辨识物件：玻璃杯、歌者、声波环、碎裂纹。

pos.zh: 共振；共鸣；回响（可数或不可数）

senses.title: Driven vibration at a natural frequency
senses.titleCN: 在固有频率下被驱动的强振动
senses.definition: the large vibration that occurs when a system is pushed at the rate it naturally prefers
senses.definitionCN: 当系统被以它天然偏好的速率推动时出现的剧烈振动
senses.example: The bridge collapsed when wind matched its resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 风与桥的共振相合时，桥塌了。
senses.why: Latin resonare means 'to sound again', and a system driven at its own rate answers every push with a larger one, so the name records the answering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语意为「再次发声」，而被以自身速率驱动的系统会对每一次推动给出更大的回应，名字记下的正是这种回应。

senses.title: A deep, full sound
senses.definition: the rich, prolonged quality of a sound that seems to fill a space
senses.definitionCN: 一种似乎填满空间的丰厚而持久的声音品质
senses.example: The cello's low strings have a warm resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴的低音弦有温暖的共鸣。
senses.why: A body that answers many frequencies at once sounds full, so the physical response became a word for tonal richness.
senses.whyCN: 能同时应和许多频率的物体听起来饱满，因此物理响应成了音色丰厚的说法。

senses.title: Magnetic resonance imaging
senses.definition: the technique in which atomic nuclei in a magnetic field absorb and re-emit radio waves at characteristic frequencies
senses.definitionCN: 原子核在磁场中于特征频率吸收并再发射无线电波的技术
senses.example: The scan uses magnetic resonance to map soft tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 这项扫描利用磁共振来成像软组织。
senses.why: Nuclei are tiny magnets with fixed precession rates, and flipping them at exactly that rate is resonance in the strict physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 原子核是带固定进动速率的小磁体，恰好在那个速率上把它翻转，就是严格物理意义上的共振。

senses.title: Resonance in chemical bonding
senses.definition: the description of a molecule as a weighted blend of several possible electron arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 把分子描述为几种可能电子排布的加权混合
senses.example: Benzene is drawn as resonance between two ring structures.
senses.exampleCN: 苯被画成两种环状结构之间的共振。
senses.why: Chemists borrowed the word because the true electron pattern behaves like a system answering several forms at once.
senses.whyCN: 化学家借这个词，是因为真实的电子分布像同时应和几种形式的系统。

senses.title: Emotional or cultural echo
senses.definition: the quality of an idea, story or image that stirs a strong shared response in an audience
senses.definitionCN: 一个想法、故事或形象在受众中激起强烈共同回应的品质
senses.example: The film found resonance with readers who had also left home.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在同样离家的读者中引起了共鸣。
senses.why: Sympathetic vibration is a ready metaphor for a feeling that is set off in one person by something in another.
senses.whyCN: 应和振动天然适合比喻一种由他人之物在自身激起的感受。

senses.title: Regular gravitational timing
senses.definition: a situation in which orbiting bodies repeatedly pull on one another in a fixed rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 轨道上的天体以固定节律反复相互牵引的情形
senses.example: The moons are locked in orbital resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 这些卫星被锁在轨道共振之中。
senses.why: The repeated gravitational pushes arrive at the same phase of each orbit, which is the astronomical version of driving a system at its own rate.
senses.whyCN: 反复的引力推动落在每次轨道的同一相位上，这正是「以自身速率驱动系统」的天文版本。

senses.title: A short-lived particle state
senses.definition: a very brief particle state that appears as a peak in a scattering experiment
senses.definitionCN: 在散射实验里表现为峰值的极短暂粒子状态
senses.example: The team reported a new resonance in the collision data.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在碰撞数据中报告了一个新的共振态。
senses.why: A particle that lives too briefly to be seen leaves a peak at one energy, the same signature as a driven oscillator.
senses.whyCN: 寿命短到看不见的粒子会在某一能量处留下峰值，其印记与受驱振子相同。

senses.title: Tuned response in a circuit
senses.definition: the condition in which an electrical circuit responds most strongly at one chosen frequency
senses.definitionCN: 电路在某一选定频率上响应最强的状态
senses.example: The radio circuit reaches resonance at the station's frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机电路在电台频率上达到共振。
senses.why: Capacitance and inductance exchange energy in a rhythm, and matching an incoming signal to that rhythm is electrical resonance.
senses.whyCN: 电容与电感按节律交换能量，把来信号与这一节律相合，就是电学共振。

intro.en: Resonance comes from Latin resonantia 'echo', from resonare 'to sound again', built on re- 'again' and sonare 'to sound'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: resonance 来自拉丁 resonantia「回声」，而它出自 resonare「再次发声」，由「再次」与「发声」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sonus meant 'sound, tone'. Its deeper origin is not established; the usual link to a root meaning 'to sound' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: sonus 意为「声音、音调」。其更早来源没有定论；把它与表示「发声」的词根联系起来的说法属于重构。

items.en: Resonare meant 'to resound, to return a sound', as a hall or a cave returns a shout.
items.cn: resonare 意为「回响、把声音送回来」，如厅堂或洞穴把喊声送回。

items.en: The noun resonantia named an echo or a re-echoing, the abstract result of that returning sound.
items.cn: 名词 resonantia 指回声或反复回响，是那种返回之声的抽象结果。

items.en: English borrowed resonance in the sixteenth century for an echoing sound, and it remained chiefly a word about acoustics.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 resonance，指回响的声音，长期主要是声学词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century physics applied it to any system driven at its natural rate, and chemistry, astronomy and medicine each took a share.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，物理学把它用于任何被自身速率驱动的系统，化学、天文学与医学各取一支。

items.en: First dates for the technical senses are approximate; the Latin chain is fully recorded.
items.cn: 各技术义的最早年代为约数；拉丁语链条有完整记录。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words and one dangerous look-alike from a different root; group two holds near sound and vibration words.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词与一个来自不同词根的易混形近词；第二组是邻近的声音与振动词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing something that resounds or is driven at its natural rate; it is not a separate physical effect.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物回响或在其固有速率上被驱动的形容词；它不是另一种物理效应。

entries.definition: From Latin residere 'to remain sitting', built on sedere 'to sit': a place where one lives, with no sound involved.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「留在坐着」，构于「坐」：指居住之所，与声音无关。

entries.definition: Latin con- 'together' plus sonare: sounds that agree when played together, a musical judgement rather than a driven vibration.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁「共同」加「发声」：合奏时相合的声音，是音乐判断而非受驱振动。

entries.definition: Latin dis- 'apart' plus sonare: sounds that clash, the opposite judgement to consonance and unrelated to resonance.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁「分开」加「发声」：相冲的声音，与「协和」相反，也与共振无关。

entries.definition: A sound reflected back once from a surface; resonance is a sustained response, not a single bounce.
entries.definitionCN: 声音从一个表面反射回来一次；而这个词指持续响应，不是一次反弹。

entries.definition: The prolonging of sound by repeated reflections in a room; it is the acoustic result that resonance can help produce.
entries.definitionCN: 声音在室内经多次反射而延长；它是共振可能促成的声学结果。

entries.definition: Any rapid back-and-forth movement; resonance is the special case where the movement grows because it is driven at the right rate.
entries.definitionCN: 任何快速的往复运动；这个词是其特例，因被以正确速率驱动而增大。

entries.definition: A feeling shared with another person; the word was once used for physical sympathetic vibration and now mostly means emotional agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人共享的感受；这个词曾用于物理上的应和振动，如今多指情感上的相合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin re- 'again' plus sonare 'to sound': a sound that answers again and again.
normal.cn: 拉丁「再次」加「发声」：一再应答的声音。

normal.en: The family runs resonance, resonant, resonate, resonator, resonantly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括共振、洪亮的、共鸣、共鸣器、以共鸣的方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: magnetic resonance, resonance frequency, emotional resonance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：磁共振、共振频率、情感共鸣。

normal.en: The same sound-root appears in consonant and dissonant, both judgements of harmony.
normal.cn: 同一「发声」词根出现在协和与不协和里，两者都是对和声的判断。

normal.en: Beware residence: it comes from sitting, not sounding, and only looks alike.
normal.cn: 当心那个表示「居住」的形近词：它出自「坐」而非「发声」，只是长得像。

abstract.en: Picture a swing pushed at exactly the moment it comes back, so each push adds height.
abstract.cn: 想象秋千荡回的那一刻恰好被推一下，于是每一推都增加高度。

abstract.en: Picture a room that repeats a single note until the note seems to own the space.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间反复送回同一个音，直到那个音仿佛占有了空间。

abstract.en: Picture two tuning forks of the same pitch, one waking the other without being touched.
abstract.cn: 想象两支同音高的音叉，一支未被触碰却唤醒了另一支。

examples.en: The singer broke the glass by finding its resonance.
examples.cn: 歌手找到玻璃的共振点，把它唱碎了。

examples.en: The poem has a resonance that outlasts its century.
examples.cn: 这首诗有一种超越它那个时代的共鸣。

examples.en: The circuit is tuned to resonance at one frequency only.
examples.cn: 这个电路只在一个频率上被调到共振。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ son（声）+ ance」——声音一再回来，就是共鸣

root: 拉丁 resonantia「回声」← resonare「再次发声」= re-「再次」+ sonare「发声」；sonus「声音」更早来源不确定。英语 resonance。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one pattern of answering: a driven system, a full tone, a medical scan, a chemical blend, an emotional echo, an orbital rhythm, a particle peak and a tuned circuit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个「应答」模式：受驱系统、饱满音色、医学扫描、化学混合、情感回声、轨道节律、粒子峰值与调谐电路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note that matches a glass's own rhythm, so every push arrives at the right moment and the swing grows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个与玻璃固有节律相合的音，每次推动都恰好落在对的时刻，摆幅便越来越大。

branches.en: THE DRIVEN SYSTEM: a glass and a radio circuit both grow loud when pushed at their own rate.
branches.cn: 受驱系统：玻璃杯与收音机电路在被以自身速率推动时都会变得强烈。

branches.en: THE FULL VOICE: a body answering many rates at once sounds rich and prolonged.
branches.cn: 饱满的声音：同时应和许多速率的物体听起来丰厚而持久。

branches.en: THE MEASURED PEAK: nuclei and short-lived particles both mark resonance as a sharp maximum in a scan.
branches.cn: 被测的峰：原子核与短命粒子都把共振表现为扫描图上的尖峰。

branches.en: THE BLEND: chemistry uses the word for a molecule that answers several electron arrangements at once.
branches.cn: 混合：化学用这个词指同时应和几种电子排布的分子。

branches.en: THE RHYTHM ELSEWHERE: a story stirs a shared feeling, and moons pull one another in step.
branches.cn: 别处的节律：故事激起共同感受，卫星则同步相互牵引。

intro.en: Resonance is a Latin abstract noun built from a prefix, a verb of sounding and a noun ending, all three of which recur in English.
intro.cn: resonance 是拉丁抽象名词，由前缀、发声动词与名词结尾构成，三者在英语里都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sonare and sonus also give consonant, dissonant, sonata and sonar's namesake; re- adds the idea of return.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sonare 与 sonus 还衍生出 consonant、dissonant、sonata 以及 sonar 的同源成分；re- 增添「返回」之意。

items.example: The prefix marks a movement that comes back.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出折返的运动。

items.example: The verb covers any sounding, sung or struck.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词涵盖任何发声，唱或敲皆可。

items.example: The noun names the thing that returns.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被送回来的那个东西。

items.example: The hall resounded with the choir.
The noun names the state of answering sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指声音应答的状态。

items.example: The note found the glass's resonance.
items.exampleCN: 那个音找到了玻璃的共振点。

items.example: A resonant voice fills the hall.

items.meaning: to echo; to strike a shared feeling
items.example: The story resonated with the audience.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事在听众中引起共鸣。

latinEntries.structure: sonare, sono, sonavi, sonatum (v., first conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to sound, to make a noise

definition_en: a place people go for holidays, or the use of something as a last option
core_image: 海边一排小屋，人们拖着行李来这里放松几天
scene: 旺季时这座海滨度假胜地挤满了来自北方的游客。In high season the seaside resort is crowded with visitors from the north.
sceneCN: 这里 resort 是「度假胜地」（第 1 个义项：人们去度假的地方）；句意：旺季时这座海滨度假胜地挤满了来自北方的游客。

pos.zh: 度假胜地；手段；应急办法

senses.title: A place for holidays
senses.definition: a place where many people go to relax on holiday
senses.definitionCN: 许多人前往放松度假的地方
senses.example: The seaside resort is crowded in high season.
senses.exampleCN: 旺季时这座海滨度假胜地很拥挤。
senses.why: A resort is first a place people turn to for rest and pleasure.
senses.whyCN: resort 首先指人们为了休息和享乐而前往的地方。

senses.title: A last option or means
senses.definition: something used because no better option is available
senses.definitionCN: 因为没有更好选择而采用的办法
senses.example: As a last resort, we can walk home.
senses.exampleCN: 实在不行，我们可以走回家。
senses.why: The place one turns to becomes any resource one turns to in difficulty.
senses.whyCN: 所前往的地方，变成困难时所求助的任何手段。

senses.title: To turn to something for help
senses.definition: to use something, often reluctantly, because it is the only way left
senses.definitionCN: 因别无他法而使用某物，常带不情愿
senses.example: They had to resort to legal action.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不得不诉诸法律行动。
senses.why: The verb keeps the image of turning toward a place of help.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留「转向求助之处」的意象。

intro.en: Resort comes from Old French resort, a place resorted to, from resortir, to go back or go out again.
intro.cn: resort 来自古法语 resort（人们常去之处），源于 resortir（再出去、返回）。

items.en: Sortir means to go out.
items.cn: sortir 意为出去。

items.en: Resortir means to go back or come out again.
items.cn: resortir 意为返回、再出去。

items.en: Resort names a place people resort to.
items.cn: resort 指人们常去的地方。

items.en: Middle English resort means a place of assembly or help.
items.cn: 中古英语 resort 指聚集或求助之处。

items.en: Resort is used for places of holiday and pleasure.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，resort 用于度假与游乐之地。

items.en: Modern English adds the phrase as a last resort.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了 as a last resort 这一说法。

note.en: Resort is a turning-to word, and it sits near its family and near words for destinations and options.
note.cn: resort 是一个「转向」词，与自身词族以及表示目的地和选择的词相邻。

entries.definition: third person form of resort
entries.definitionCN: resort 的第三人称单数形式

entries.definition: past form of resort
a person who often visits resorts
the place someone is travelling to
a choice available in a situation
a place of safety or help

normalIntro.en: Resort is a place one turns to: first a holiday place, then any last option.
normalIntro.cn: resort 是人转向的地方：先指度假地，再指任何最后手段。

normal.en: The verb resort to means turn to something for help.
normal.cn: 动词 resort to 意为求助于某物。

normal.en: A seaside resort is a place people travel to.
normal.cn: seaside resort 是人们前往的海滨度假地。

normal.en: As a last resort marks the final option.
normal.cn: as a last resort 标记最后的选择。

normal.en: The same word covers a place and a choice.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指地方，也指选择。

normal.en: Compare destination: destination is neutral, while resort suggests leisure.
normal.cn: 对比 destination：destination 中性，resort 带有休闲意味。

abstract.en: Picture suitcases rolling along a promenade.
abstract.cn: 想象行李箱沿着海滨步道滚动。

abstract.en: Imagine an empty road leading to the only open door.
abstract.cn: 想象一条空路通向唯一还开着的门。

abstract.en: Think of a hand reaching for the last tool in a box.
abstract.cn: 想象手伸向盒子里最后一件工具。

examples.en: The seaside resort is crowded in high season.
examples.cn: 旺季时这座海滨度假胜地很拥挤。

examples.en: As a last resort, we can walk home.
examples.cn: 实在不行，我们可以走回家。

examples.en: They had to resort to legal action.
examples.cn: 他们不得不诉诸法律行动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + sort」——再次出发去某个地方，先想到的是度假地，最后才当作手段；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 sortir（出去）→ resortir（返回、再出去）→ resort（人们常去之处）→ 中古英语 resort → 现代英语 resort。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a place people travel to for rest, then becomes any option people turn to when nothing better remains.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从人们前往休息的地方开始，再变成别无更好选择时所求助的任何手段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a place people turn toward for rest or help.
core.cn: 核心意象：人们为了休息或求助而转向的地方。

branches.en: A holiday place is the most concrete sense.
branches.cn: 度假地，是最具体的义项。

branches.en: A last option is the place image turned abstract.
branches.cn: 最后手段，是「地方」意象的抽象化。

branches.en: The verb describes turning to that option.
branches.cn: 动词描述转向那个办法。

branches.en: People travel to a resort, and people turn to a last resort.
branches.cn: 人们前往度假地，也转向最后手段。

branches.en: The option and the act of using it are two sides of the same word.
branches.cn: 办法与使用办法的行为是同一个词的两面。

intro.en: Resort is a French noun and verb that English reshaped, and its small family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: resort 是经英语改造的法语名词兼动词，小词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The French verb sortir means to go out, and resortir means to come back or go out again; the Latin prefix re- adds the return.
latinIntro.cn: 法语动词 sortir 意为出去，resortir 意为返回或再出去；拉丁前缀 re- 增添「返回」。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of returning.

items.meaning: to go back, come out again
items.example: Resortir joins the prefix and the verb.
items.exampleCN: resortir 把前缀与动词结合。

items.meaning: a holiday place or last option
items.example: Resort keeps both place and option senses.
items.exampleCN: resort 保留场所与办法两种含义。

items.example: Seaside resort is a common compound.
items.exampleCN: seaside resort 是常见复合词。

definition_en: something useful that can be used to achieve a goal
core_image: 仓库里整齐码放着工具、材料和食物，随时可以取用
scene: 岛上淡水有限，居民很早就学会珍惜每一份资源。Fresh water is limited on the island, so residents learned early to value every resource.
sceneCN: 这里 resource 是「资源」（第 1 个义项：可利用的有用之物）；句意：岛上淡水有限，居民很早就学会珍惜每一份资源。

senses.title: A useful supply
senses.definition: a supply of something such as water, fuel, or money that can be used
senses.definitionCN: 水、燃料或资金等可供使用的供应
senses.example: The country is rich in natural resources.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家自然资源丰富。
senses.why: The word names a source to which one can return for help.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指可以反复回来求助的来源。

senses.title: Personal ability to cope
senses.definition: the ability to find a way through a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 在困难处境中找到出路的能力
senses.example: She showed great resource in a crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 她在危机中表现出很强的应变能力。
senses.why: A person's inner reserves are a resource drawn on in trouble.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的内在储备，就是困难时可取用的资源。

senses.title: A teaching or reference material
senses.definition: a book, website, or other material used for learning or reference
senses.definitionCN: 用于学习或查阅的书、网站或其他材料
senses.example: The website is a useful resource for teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站对教师来说是很有用的资源。
senses.why: Any material one can draw on for a task is a resource.
senses.whyCN: 任何可供任务取用的材料都是资源。

intro.en: Resource comes from French ressource, a source of help, from Old French resourdre, to rise again, ultimately Latin resurgere.
intro.cn: resource 来自法语 ressource（求助之源），源于古法语 resourdre（重新升起），最终来自拉丁语 resurgere。

items.en: Surgere means to rise.
items.cn: surgere 意为升起。

items.en: Resurgere means to rise again.
items.cn: resurgere 意为重新升起。

items.en: Resourdre means to rise again or recover.
items.cn: resourdre 意为再起、恢复。

items.en: Ressource means a source of help or recovery.
items.cn: ressource 意为求助或恢复的来源。

items.en: English resource covers means of support and available supplies.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，英语 resource 涵盖支持手段与可用物资。

items.en: Modern English often uses the plural for a country's wealth.
items.cn: 现代英语常用复数指一个国家的财富。

note.en: Resource is a source one draws on, and it sits near its family and near words for supplies and means.
note.cn: resource 是一个可取用的来源，与自身词族以及表示供应和手段的词相邻。

entries.definition: good at finding ways to solve problems
in a clever and practical way
the ability to cope cleverly
an amount of something available
something valuable that can be used
a method or resource for doing something

normalIntro.en: Resource is a source one can rise back to: something useful kept ready.
normalIntro.cn: resource 是一个可以回头依靠的来源：随时备好的有用之物。

normal.en: The re- suggests rising again when needed.
normal.cn: re- 暗示需要时能再站起来。

normal.en: Natural resources are supplies taken from the earth.
normal.cn: 自然资源取自大地。

normal.en: Human resources are the people an organisation can draw on.
normal.cn: 人力资源是组织可以依靠的人。

normal.en: A resourceful person finds a way with very little.
normal.cn: resourceful 的人用很少的东西也能找到办法。

normal.en: Compare source: a source supplies, while a resource is a source you can use.
normal.cn: 对比 source：source 提供来源，resource 是可供你使用的来源。

abstract.en: Picture shelves of tools and food neatly stacked.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上整齐放着工具和食物。

abstract.en: Imagine a small boat with one oar used cleverly.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小船，靠一支桨巧妙前行。

abstract.en: Think of a teacher's box of ready-made materials.
abstract.cn: 想象老师一盒备好的教学材料。

examples.en: The country is rich in natural resources.
examples.cn: 这个国家自然资源丰富。

examples.en: She showed great resource in a crisis.
examples.cn: 她在危机中表现出很强的应变能力。

examples.en: The website is a useful resource for teachers.
examples.cn: 这个网站对教师来说是很有用的资源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + source」——可以反复回去取用的来源，就是资源；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 surgere（升起）→ resurgere（再起）→ 古法语 resourdre → ressource（求助之源）→ 现代英语 resource。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a source of help one can return to, then covers material supplies, inner coping ability, and learning materials.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从可以回去求助的来源开始，再涵盖物资储备、内在应变能力与学习材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a store of useful things ready to be drawn on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一批随时可取用的有用之物。

branches.en: Material supply is the basic modern sense.
branches.cn: 物资供应，是基本现代义项。

branches.en: Inner ability is a resource stored in a person.
branches.cn: 内在能力，是储存在人身上的资源。

branches.en: Learning material is a resource drawn on for a task.
branches.cn: 学习材料是为任务取用的资源。

branches.en: Countries and people both draw on reserves in hard times.
branches.cn: 国家与人都会在困难时动用储备。

branches.en: A clever person and a good website both help solve problems.
branches.cn: 聪明的人与好网站都能帮助解决问题。

intro.en: Resource is a French-shaped noun built on the Latin verb for rising again, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: resource 是建立在拉丁语「再起」动词上的法语形态名词，词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin surgere means to rise, and resurgere means to rise again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 surgere 意为升起，resurgere 意为重新升起。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of rising again.
Resurgere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: resurgere 把前缀与词根结合。

items.example: Resourdre carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: resourdre 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Ressource is the direct source of resource.
items.exampleCN: ressource 是 resource 的直接来源。
resource 保留「求助之源」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾

definition_en: a feeling of admiration, or a particular aspect of something
core_image: 一个人后退半步，认真看着对方，身体微微前倾
scene: 那位老教师走进教室时，所有学生都站起来表示敬意。When the old teacher entered the classroom, every student stood up to show respect.
sceneCN: 这里 respect 是「敬意」（第 1 个义项：对某人怀有的钦佩与重视）；句意：老教师走进教室时，所有学生都站起来表示敬意。

senses.title: Admiration and esteem
senses.definition: a feeling of admiration for someone because of their qualities or achievements
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的品质或成就而钦佩他
senses.example: Every student stood up to show respect.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都站起来表示敬意。
senses.why: The Latin word means a looking back at someone, and that look becomes esteem.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为回头注视某人，这种注视就变成敬意。

senses.title: A particular aspect
senses.definition: one detail or point in which things can be compared
senses.definitionCN: 事物可以相互比较的某个细节或要点
senses.example: In this respect, the two plans are alike.
senses.exampleCN: 在这方面，两项计划很相似。
senses.why: Looking back at a thing can mean looking at one particular side of it.
senses.whyCN: 「回头看某物」也可以指看它的某一个侧面。

senses.title: To admire and treat well
senses.definition: to admire someone and treat them with care and fairness
senses.definitionCN: 钦佩某人并以体贴、公平的方式对待他
senses.example: She respects her teacher greatly.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常尊敬她的老师。
senses.why: The noun's esteem becomes the verb's way of acting toward someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词的「敬意」变成动词对待某人的方式。

intro.en: Respect comes from Latin respectus, a looking back, from respicere, to look back at, built on re- and specere, to look.
intro.cn: respect 来自拉丁语 respectus（回顾），源于 respicere（回头看），由 re- 与 specere（看）构成。

items.en: Specere means to look at.
items.cn: specere 意为看。

items.en: Respicere means to look back at or consider.
items.cn: respicere 意为回头看、考虑。

items.en: Respectus means a looking back or regard.
items.cn: respectus 意为回顾、注目。

items.en: Respect means regard or consideration.
items.cn: respect 意为重视、考虑。

items.en: Middle English respect covers esteem and a particular point.
items.cn: 中古英语 respect 兼指敬意与某个方面。

items.en: Modern English uses respect as both noun and verb.
items.cn: 现代英语中，respect 兼作名词与动词。

note.en: Respect is a looking-back word, and it sits near its family and near words for esteem and regard.
note.cn: respect 是一个「回头看」的词，与自身词族以及表示敬重和关注的词相邻。

entries.definition: showing respect
in a respectful way
belonging separately to each one
great respect and admiration
respect or attention for someone
public respect or a mark of it

normalIntro.en: Respect contains specere, to look: respect begins with looking at someone properly.
normalIntro.cn: respect 含有 specere（看）：尊重始于认真注视对方。

normal.en: Re- means back, and specere means look: to look back with regard.
normal.cn: re- 表示回，specere 表示看：带着重视回头看。

normal.en: Show respect is the common phrase.
normal.cn: show respect 是常见短语。

normal.en: In this respect means in this particular aspect.
normal.cn: in this respect 意为「在这方面」。

normal.en: Respectful is the adjective for showing regard.
normal.cn: respectful 是表示「恭敬的」形容词。

normal.en: Compare esteem: esteem is admiration, while respect also includes fair treatment.
normal.cn: 对比 esteem：esteem 是钦佩，respect 还包括公平对待。

abstract.en: Picture a student standing as a teacher enters.
abstract.cn: 想象老师进门时学生站起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a listener putting down the phone to look at you.
abstract.cn: 想象听者放下手机，认真看着你。

abstract.en: Think of a slight bow before a serious conversation.
abstract.cn: 想象严肃谈话前微微躬身。

examples.en: Every student stood up to show respect.
examples.cn: 每个学生都站起来表示敬意。

examples.en: In this respect, the two plans are alike.
examples.cn: 在这方面，两项计划很相似。

examples.en: She respects her teacher greatly.
examples.cn: 她非常尊敬她的老师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + spect」——回头再看一眼，是因为心里看重，所以尊重；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 specere（看）→ respicere（回头看）→ respectus（回顾、注目）→ 古法语 respect → 现代英语 respect。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a backward look of regard, which becomes esteem, then a particular side of a thing, and finally the way one treats another person.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从带着重视的回头注视开始，变成敬意，再指事物的某个侧面，最后指对待他人的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pausing to look at someone with attention and care.
core.cn: 核心意象：停下来，带着关注与体贴看着某人。

branches.en: Esteem is the feeling produced by that careful look.
branches.cn: 敬意是由认真注视产生的感受。

branches.en: A respect is one side of a thing seen closely.
branches.cn: 「方面」是近距离观察到的某个侧面。

branches.en: The verb turns esteem into fair treatment.
branches.cn: 动词把敬意变成公平对待。

branches.en: Feeling respect and acting respectfully belong together.
branches.cn: 心怀敬意与以礼相待彼此相连。

branches.en: Attention to detail and attention to people share the same look.
branches.cn: 关注细节与关注他人共享同一种注视。

intro.en: Respect is a Latin noun and verb carried through French, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: respect 是经法语传递的拉丁名词兼动词，词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere means to look, and respicere means to look back at or consider.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere 意为看，respicere 意为回头看、考虑。

items.exampleCN: re- 增添「回头看」的意思。

items.example: Respicere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: respicere 把前缀与词根结合。

items.example: Respective shares the same Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: respective 共享同一拉丁词干。

definition_en: belonging separately to each person or thing mentioned
core_image: 几个人走回各自的门口，每扇门只属于一个人
scene: 会议结束后，两位经理回到了各自的办公室。After the meeting, the two managers returned to their respective offices.
sceneCN: 这里 respective 是「各自的」（第 1 个义项：分别属于先前提到的人或物）；句意：会议结束后，两位经理各自回到自己的办公室。

senses.title: Belonging to each separately
senses.definition: relating to each of the people or things already mentioned, one by one
senses.definitionCN: 逐一与已经提到的每个人或每件事相关的
senses.example: The students returned to their respective classrooms.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们回到了各自的教室。
senses.why: The word began as a relative term meaning looking back to each item, so it pairs things with their own owners.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是关系词，意为逐一回看每一项，因此把事物与各自的所有者配对。

senses.title: Separate rather than shared
senses.definition: used to stress that each item has its own separate one
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调每一项都有自己单独的一份
senses.example: Each team presented its respective plan.
senses.exampleCN: 每支队伍都展示了自己那份方案。
senses.why: If every item looks back to its own partner, the result is a set of separate belongings.
senses.whyCN: 如果每一项都对应自己的伙伴，结果就是一整套各自归属之物。

intro.en: Respective comes from Latin respectivus, looking back, from respicere, to look back at, built on re-, back, and specere, to look.
intro.cn: respective 来自拉丁语 respectivus（回看的），源于 respicere（回看），由 re-（向后）与 specere（看）构成。

items.en: Specere means to look.
items.cn: specere 意为看。

items.en: Respicere means to look back at.
items.cn: respicere 意为回看。

items.en: Respectivus means relating or looking back.
items.cn: respectivus 意为有关联的、回看的。

items.en: Respectif carries the relative sense.
items.cn: respectif 保留「各自相关」的含义。

items.en: Modern English uses respective to pair items with their own owners.
items.cn: 现代英语用 respective 把各项与各自的所有者配对。

note.en: Respective is a pairing adjective, close to respectively and to words for separate ownership.
note.cn: respective 是表示配对的形容词，与 respectively 以及表示各自所有的词相邻。

entries.definition: in the order already mentioned
admiration or a particular point
showing respect
belonging to one person or thing
not shared
belonging to a particular person

normalIntro.en: Respective points back to each item: this one to its owner, that one to its owner.
normalIntro.cn: respective 逐一回指每一项：这个对应它的主人，那个对应它的主人。

normal.en: Their respective rooms means each person's own room.
normal.cn: their respective rooms 指每个人的房间。

normal.en: Respective roles are the roles each person has.
normal.cn: respective roles 是每个人各自承担的角色。

normal.en: The adverb respectively keeps the same order.
normal.cn: 副词 respectively 保持同样的顺序。

normal.en: Respective never means respectful.
normal.cn: respective 绝不表示「恭敬的」。

normal.en: Compare separate: separate stresses division, respective stresses matching each item.
normal.cn: 对比 separate：separate 强调分开，respective 强调逐项对应。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking to two different doors.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人走向两扇不同的门。

abstract.en: Imagine two name tags placed on two different chairs.
abstract.cn: 想象两个名牌分别放在两把不同的椅子上。

abstract.en: Think of two arrows pointing to two separate boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象两个箭头分别指向两个不同的盒子。

examples.en: The two sides set out their respective views.
examples.cn: 双方各自陈述了自己的观点。

examples.en: Each member returned to their respective seat.
examples.cn: 每位成员都回到了各自的座位。

examples.en: The report compares the respective costs of the two plans.
examples.cn: 报告比较了两个方案各自的成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「respect + ive」——每个人都被「单独看一眼」，就是各自的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）＋ specere（看）→ respicere（回看）→ respectivus（有关的）→ 英语 respective，核心义「逐一对应、各自归属」。

sensesIntro.en: Respective first pairs each mentioned item with its own owner, and then stresses that these owners are separate.
sensesIntro.cn: respective 先把提到的每一项与自己的所有者配对，再强调这些所有者彼此分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: arrows from each item to its own owner.
core.cn: 核心意象：从每一项指向其各自所有者的箭头。

branches.en: Pairing each item with its owner is the core sense.
branches.cn: 把每一项与所有者配对是核心义项。

branches.en: Separateness is the emphasis the adjective often carries.
branches.cn: 分开是这个词常带的强调。

branches.en: Each has a separate item, and each item belongs to its own person.
branches.cn: 每人有单独的一份，每份又属于各自的人。

branches.en: The pair may be two people, two plans, or two rooms.
branches.cn: 配对对象可以是两个人、两个方案或两个房间。

branches.en: Even when the items look alike, they remain respective ones.
branches.cn: 即使物品看起来相似，它们仍是各自的东西。

intro.en: Respective belongs to the specere family of looking words, with English respect, respectful, and respectively.
intro.cn: respective 属于 specere（看）词族，英语亲属有 respect、respectful 与 respectively。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere means to look, and respicere means to look back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere 意为看，respicere 意为回看。

definition_zh: 呼吸；呼吸作用；一次呼吸；（生物的）气体交换
definition_en: the act or process of breathing, or in biology the exchange of gases between an organism and its environment and the release of energy from food
core_image: 胸腔一起一伏，空气从口鼻进入肺部，再带着二氧化碳出来
scene: 这里指「呼吸」。 Respiration slows during deep sleep as the body needs less oxygen.
sceneCN: 这里 respiration 指「呼吸动作」（第 1 个义项：吸进氧气、呼出二氧化碳的生理动作）；句意：深度睡眠时呼吸变慢，因为身体需要的氧气减少。图中可辨识物件：胸腔轮廓、肺、气流箭头、睡眠监测仪。

pos.zh: 呼吸；呼吸作用；一次呼吸；气体交换（指过程时不可数，指一次呼吸时可用复数 respirations）

senses.title: Breathing in and out
senses.definition: the physical act of drawing air into the lungs and letting it out again
senses.definitionCN: 把空气吸入肺再呼出的身体动作
senses.example: Respiration slows during deep sleep as the body needs less oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 深度睡眠时呼吸变慢，因为身体需要的氧气减少。
senses.why: Latin respirare meant 'to breathe again'; the noun starts as the repeated cycle of taking air and giving it back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 respirare 意为「再次呼吸」；这个名词的起点是吸气与还气的反复循环。

senses.title: Gas exchange
senses.titleCN: 气体交换：氧气进入、二氧化碳排出
senses.definition: the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between blood and air in the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 血液与肺泡空气之间氧气与二氧化碳的交换
senses.example: External respiration takes place across the alveolar membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 外呼吸发生在肺泡膜两侧。
senses.why: Physiology separated the visible movement of the chest from the chemical exchange it serves.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把可见的胸廓运动与它所服务的化学交换区分开来。

senses.title: Cellular respiration
senses.titleCN: 细胞呼吸：细胞分解有机物释放能量
senses.definition: the chemical process in cells that releases energy from glucose, usually using oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 细胞内分解葡萄糖释放能量的化学过程，通常使用氧气
senses.example: Cellular respiration turns glucose into ATP and carbon dioxide.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞呼吸把葡萄糖变成 ATP 与二氧化碳。
senses.why: The same word scales down from the lungs to the mitochondrion, because both are exchanges of gases and energy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从肺缩小到线粒体，因为两者都是气体与能量的交换。

senses.title: One breath
senses.titleCN: 一次呼吸：一吸一呼的计数单位
senses.definition: a single cycle of inhalation and exhalation, used as a countable unit
senses.definitionCN: 一次吸气与呼气的完整循环，作可数单位使用
senses.example: The patient takes about twelve respirations a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人每分钟大约呼吸十二次。
senses.why: The countable sense comes from counting cycles, the way heartbeat is counted.
senses.whyCN: 可数义来自对循环的计数，计数方式与心跳相同。

senses.title: Respiratory capacity
senses.titleCN: 呼吸功能：完成气体交换的能力
senses.definition: the ability of a person or organism to carry out breathing and gas exchange
senses.definitionCN: 人或生物完成呼吸与气体交换的能力
senses.example: Illness reduced her respiration and she needed oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病削弱了她的呼吸功能，需要吸氧。
senses.why: As with many action nouns, the process can stand for the capacity to perform it.
senses.whyCN: 与许多动作名词一样，过程可以代指完成该过程的能力。

senses.title: Artificial respiration
senses.titleCN: 人工呼吸：替他人维持通气
senses.definition: the act of helping or replacing someone's breathing by machine or by mouth
senses.definitionCN: 用机器或口对口方式帮助或替代他人呼吸
senses.example: Artificial respiration kept him alive until the ambulance arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 人工呼吸让他撑到救护车到来。
senses.why: Emergency medicine turned the noun into a fixed phrase for a life-saving substitute action.
senses.whyCN: 急救医学把这个名词变成固定短语，指一种救命的替代动作。

senses.title: Plant respiration
senses.titleCN: 植物呼吸：植物同样吸氧放二氧化碳
senses.definition: in botany, the uptake of oxygen and release of carbon dioxide by plant cells, day and night
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指植物细胞昼夜吸收氧气并释放二氧化碳
senses.example: Root respiration uses oxygen from the air spaces in soil.
senses.exampleCN: 根系呼吸使用土壤空隙中的氧气。
senses.why: Botany needed the term to correct the old belief that plants only produce oxygen.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要这个词来纠正「植物只产氧」的旧看法。

senses.title: A living metaphor
senses.titleCN: 拟人用法：森林或城市的「呼吸」
senses.definition: figuratively, the visible rhythm of breathing attributed to a place or a large system
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，把呼吸的节律赋予一个地方或一个庞大系统
senses.example: You can feel the slow respiration of the forest at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分，你能感到森林缓慢的呼吸。
senses.why: Writers lend the bodily rhythm to landscapes, because a forest also exchanges gases on a vast scale.
senses.whyCN: 作家把身体的节律借给风景，因为森林同样在巨大尺度上交换气体。

senses.title: Anaerobic respiration
senses.titleCN: 无氧呼吸：没有氧气也能释放能量
senses.definition: energy release from food without oxygen, producing lactate, ethanol or other products
senses.definitionCN: 无氧条件下从食物中释放能量，产生乳酸、乙醇等产物
senses.example: Anaerobic respiration in muscles produces lactate during a sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 短跑时肌肉的无氧呼吸产生乳酸。
senses.why: The word's core is exchange and energy release, so it can name a version that needs no external air at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是交换与能量释放，因此也能命名一种完全不需要外界空气的版本。

intro.en: Respiration comes from Latin respiratio, built on respirare 'to breathe again', from re- 'again' and spirare 'to breathe'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: respiration 出自拉丁 respiratio，由 respirare「再次呼吸」构成，而 respirare 来自 re-「再次」与 spirare「呼吸」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its family is wide: spiritus 'breath, spirit', inspirare 'to breathe into', expirare 'to breathe out'.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其词族很广：spiritus「气息、精神」、inspirare「吹入」、expirare「呼出」。

items.en: Respirare added re- 'again' or 'back': to breathe again, to recover breath, to take a rest. Classical Latin used it for catching one's breath after effort.
items.cn: respirare 加 re-「再次、返回」：再次呼吸、缓过气来、休息。古典拉丁用它指用力之后喘过气来。

items.en: Respiratio named the act of breathing again and, by extension, the ordinary process of breathing.
items.cn: respiratio 指再次呼吸的动作，并引申为一般的呼吸过程。

items.en: English respiration is recorded in the fourteenth century, at first as a general word for breathing and for rest after exertion.
items.cn: 英语 respiration 记录于 14 世纪，起初泛指呼吸以及用力后的歇息。

items.en: From the seventeenth century onward physiology split the word into external respiration in the lungs and internal or cellular respiration in the tissues.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，生理学把这个词分为肺内的外呼吸与组织内的内呼吸或细胞呼吸。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper Indo-European root behind spirare is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑；spirare 背后的更深印欧词根属重构形式，并非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for breathing and gas exchange.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「呼吸与气体交换」的近义词。

entries.definition: To breathe; the verb names the action, while respiration names the process or one cycle of it.
entries.definitionCN: 呼吸；动词指动作，respiration 指过程或其中的一次循环。

entries.definition: Relating to breathing, as in respiratory system; it describes organs and functions rather than the act.
entries.definitionCN: 与呼吸有关，如呼吸系统；它描述器官与功能，而非动作。

entries.definition: A mask or machine that supplies air or filters it; it is a countable object, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 供气或滤气的面罩或机器；是可数物件，不是过程。

entries.definition: Sweating through the skin; it shares the Latin spirare root but names water loss, not gas exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 经皮肤出汗；它与 respiration 共享拉丁 spirare 词根，但指失水，而非气体交换。

entries.definition: The ordinary English word for moving air in and out; respiration is the technical and biological term.
entries.definitionCN: 日常英语中「吸进呼出空气」的普通词；respiration 是技术与生物学用语。

entries.definition: The mechanical movement of air into and out of the lungs; it names the transport, while respiration includes the exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 空气进出肺的机械运动；它命名输送，而 respiration 还包括交换。

entries.definition: The transfer of oxygen and carbon dioxide across a membrane; it is the functional core of respiration.
entries.definitionCN: 氧气与二氧化碳跨膜转移，是呼吸的功能核心。

entries.definition: All the chemical reactions of a living body; cellular respiration is one part of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 生物体全部的化学反应；细胞呼吸只是代谢的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + spirare 'breathe': breathing is a cycle that repeats.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ spirare「呼吸」：呼吸是不断重复的循环。

normal.en: The family runs respire, respiratory, respirator, respirometer and respiration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 respire、respiratory、respirator、respirometer、respiration。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the science: cellular respiration, aerobic respiration, artificial respiration, external respiration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学语境：细胞呼吸、有氧呼吸、人工呼吸、外呼吸。

normal.en: spirare also gives spirit, inspire, expire and conspire.
normal.cn: spirare 还衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、conspire。

normal.en: Breathing is ventilation; the chemistry it enables is respiration.
normal.cn: 呼吸动作是 ventilation，它促成的化学过程才是 respiration。

abstract.en: Picture a tide going in and out of a chest, slow and even.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水在胸腔里进出，缓慢而均匀。

abstract.en: Picture a mitochondrion as a tiny furnace that takes sugar and oxygen and gives out energy.
abstract.cn: 想象线粒体是一座小炉子，吃进糖与氧，放出能量。

abstract.en: Picture a forest at dawn, mist moving as if the whole wood were breathing.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时的森林，雾气流动，仿佛整片树林在呼吸。

examples.en: Respiration rate is one of the vital signs recorded on admission.
examples.cn: 呼吸频率是入院时记录的生命体征之一。

examples.en: Cellular respiration releases energy stored in glucose.
examples.cn: 细胞呼吸释放储存在葡萄糖中的能量。

examples.en: Anaerobic respiration allows muscles to work without enough oxygen.
examples.cn: 无氧呼吸让肌肉在氧气不足时仍能工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re 再次 + spir 呼吸 + ation 过程」——一遍遍再呼吸 → respiration 呼吸

root: 拉丁 re-「再次」+ spirare「呼吸」→ respirare「再次呼吸、缓气」→ respiratio「呼吸」→ 英语 respiration。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one cycle: air goes in and out, the body takes oxygen and gives back carbon dioxide, and that exchange can happen in a lung, a cell, a plant or a whole forest.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个循环展开：空气进出，身体取氧还碳，而这种交换可以发生在肺里、细胞里、植物里，也可以发生在一整片森林里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air moving in and out of a body, taking oxygen and returning carbon dioxide.
core.cn: 核心意象：空气进出身体，取走氧气，还回二氧化碳。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE CYCLE: the chest movement and the single counted breath are the same event at two scales.
branches.cn: 可见的循环：胸廓运动与可计数的单次呼吸，是同一事件的两个尺度。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY: gas exchange can run with oxygen or without it, in lungs or in muscle.
branches.cn: 化学层面：气体交换可以在有氧或无氧、在肺里或肌肉里进行。

branches.en: THE CELL: the same word names the mitochondrial breakdown of glucose.
branches.cn: 细胞一端：同一个词也命名线粒体对葡萄糖的分解。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND SUBSTITUTE: the process becomes an ability, and medicine can replace it artificially.
branches.cn: 能力与替代：过程变成能力，医学也能用人工方式替代它。

branches.en: BEYOND ANIMALS: plants respire too, and writers lend the rhythm to whole landscapes.
branches.cn: 动物之外：植物也会呼吸，作家则把这个节律借给整片风景。

intro.en: Respiration is a Latin verb of breathing plus a noun of action: re- + spirare + -tio.
intro.cn: respiration 是拉丁「呼吸」动词加动作名词后缀：re- + spirare + -tio。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare 'to breathe' supplies spirit, inspire, expire, conspire and respirare; respiratio gives English respiration, respire and respiratory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare「呼吸」衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、conspire、respirare；respiratio 给出英语 respiration、respire、respiratory。

items.meaning: a device that supplies or filters air

items.exampleCN: 呼吸测量仪追踪了土壤的耗氧量。

items.example: The word spirit began as a word for breath.
items.exampleCN: spirit 最初是表示呼吸的词。
